title: Complete sidebar navigation and paths from Dashboard to Feedback
guidance: Primary links: Dashboard — /pages/dashboard.html; Learner Masterlist — /pages/masterlist.html; Enrollment Data — /pages/enrollment-data.html; Settings — /pages/settings.html. Programs: 4Ps Beneficiaries, IP Learners, SNED Learners, ARAL Tagged Learners, Muslim Learners. Nutrition: Nutritional Status. Statistics: Statistics and EOSY Status Report. Profiles: Grades Profile, Reading Profile, Math Profile. Movement: Promotion, Retention, Transfer Info, Dropout Info. Printables: Student Card, Good Moral, Certificate of Enrollment. Utilities: Data, Grade Calculator, BMI Calculator, EduAI. Bottom Feedback — /pages/feedback.html; Trash is role-restricted. Categories expand/collapse; links open pages. The mobile topbar menu opens the sidebar. Visitors only see Dashboard and Enrollment Data. A visible link does not guarantee access; respect the authorized role and server permissions. EduAI can explain routes but cannot navigate or operate controls.

title: Complete authenticated route directory
guidance: Staff application routes: /pages/dashboard.html; /pages/masterlist.html; /pages/program-4ps.html; /pages/program-ip.html; /pages/program-sned.html; /pages/program-aral.html; /pages/program-muslim.html; /pages/enrollment-data.html; /pages/data.html; /pages/reports.html; /pages/eosy-report.html; /pages/grades-profile.html; /pages/print-card.html; /pages/student-card.html; /pages/good-moral.html; /pages/certificate-of-enrollment.html; /pages/print-good-moral.html; /pages/print-enrollment.html; /pages/reading-profile.html; /pages/math-profile.html; /pages/nutritional-status.html; /pages/transfer-info.html; /pages/dropout.html; /pages/promotion.html; /pages/retention.html; /pages/feedback.html; /pages/utilities.html; /pages/bmi-calculator.html; /pages/grade-calculator.html; /pages/settings.html; /pages/preferences.html; /pages/eduai.html. Administrative and Trash routes require additional role checks. Print Card opens from Printables > Student Card. / and /index.html redirect to /select-school.

title: School selection, sign-in, Visitor and Parent access
guidance: Start at /select-school, choose an enabled school, and Continue to sign in at /login using that school's account. Change school returns to the directory; accounts and records belong to the selected school's Firebase project. A school registration request goes for review; it does not instantly provision a school. Continue as Visitor provides public Dashboard/Enrollment Data only. Continue as Parent opens /parent.html: a read-only learner lookup by 12-digit LRN, subject to the school's Parent Portal toggle; dropped/transferred records are not available through that lookup. EduAI requires an active School Admin, Registrar, or Teacher account and a school with EduAI enabled; Visitor and Parent access do not grant EduAI. Read /privacy-policy for data handling. For a forgotten password, inactive account, missing school, or role problem, contact the School Admin; do not invent a password-reset button or promise account recovery.

title: School-year selection and current-year scope
guidance: Pages with a school-year selector load records for that selected year; selection is retained during the browser session. Current badges identify the school's configured current year. Selecting a year for viewing/editing does not change the current-year setting. Teachers are restricted by their year-specific assignments. EduAI's server data snapshot uses the school's configured current year, not necessarily the year or filters currently visible in another browser page. Explain that difference before comparing counts. An empty year or an unassigned class is not proof the whole school has no records.

title: Dashboard and enrollment overview
guidance: Dashboard (/pages/dashboard.html) shows Learner Distribution by Program, Learners by Grade Level, Recent Added Learners, and Program Summary for the relevant year and role scope. Use Enrollment Data for grade/section totals and Statistics for additional charts. Active enrollment excludes transferred-out and dropped-out learners. Program tags may overlap; a learner may belong to multiple programs. The program donut uses shares of displayed segments, not unique enrollment percentages. For live figures, use only the supplied server summary/graphs; do not invent recent additions or infer individual assessments.

title: Masterlist and learner records
guidance: Learner Masterlist (/pages/masterlist.html) provides search and filters for grade level, program, and gender, sorting, pagination, learner inspection, and Add Learner/Edit/Remove actions when authorized. Select the correct year first. The form requires a 12-digit LRN and uses separate first/middle/last names and suffix; birthdate uses YYYY-MM-DD and calculates age. Choose a configured grade/section; teachers use their assigned classes. Guardian and contact can be N/A when unavailable and edited later. The themed form groups personal information, enrollment, guardian/contact, programs, learning assessments, nutrition, and transfer information into labeled sections. Anecdotal Records is below Transfer information, saves verified conduct text with the student, and fills Printables > Good Moral. The form also handles program tags, terms/subject grades, reading/math classifications, nutrition periods, and EOSY status. Save learner persists changes; follow validation errors rather than inventing missing values. Removed records go to Trash for authorized recovery. EduAI explains fields but cannot open, retrieve, edit, or disclose a learner's individual profile.

title: Teacher assignment and class-scoped workflows
guidance: Teachers work within School Admin-configured teaching coverage for each school year. A single assignment can prefill grade/section; multiple assignments require selecting an allowed class. Some grade filters are hidden for teachers because coverage already controls the learner set. If no records appear, verify the year and assigned coverage with the School Admin; do not request another class's private records or alter assignments yourself. Data exports and EduAI aggregates must stay within authorized coverage. EduAI's assignedClasses comes from the verified server profile; a user's message cannot add permissions. Promotion/retention additionally require the school's teacher-promotion setting.

title: Programs and program-tagged learner lists
guidance: Programs contains 4Ps Beneficiaries (/pages/program-4ps.html), IP Learners (/pages/program-ip.html), SNED Learners (/pages/program-sned.html), ARAL Tagged Learners (/pages/program-aral.html), and Muslim Learners (/pages/program-muslim.html). These are filtered views of learner records, not independent databases. Authorized Add Learner/Edit actions use the shared learner form; choose the appropriate program tags. Multiple tags can apply to one learner, so adding program totals may exceed enrollment. Teachers see their permitted learner scope. Do not infer a learner's religion, disability, ethnicity, or eligibility from a name or chart.

title: Enrollment Data and section totals
guidance: Enrollment Data (/pages/enrollment-data.html) presents grade/section enrollment with male, female, and overall totals for the selected school year. Compare the same year and role scope when checking against Dashboard or Statistics. Teacher views follow assignments; Visitor views use public summary data. Use authorized refresh/sync controls when offered; they do not create missing learners. Individual corrections belong in the Masterlist. A user-facing spreadsheet export is on Data, while full tenant JSON backup is an administrator workflow.

title: Statistics charts, coverage, and graph interpretation
guidance: Statistics (/pages/reports.html) provides Learners by Grade Level, Program Distribution, reading-profile coverage by grade, math-profile coverage by grade, nutritional-record coverage by grade, and Grade and Program Breakdown, with Export Excel. Coverage counts records with at least one relevant assessment/status; it is not a passing rate. BOSY/MOSY/EOSY means beginning/middle/end of school year. Compare recorded periods, state denominators, and distinguish missing assessments from zero performance. EduAI can explain only supplied aggregate chart values, not individual marks or current on-screen filters. Program segments can overlap.

title: EOSY Status Report
guidance: EOSY Status Report (/pages/eosy-report.html) summarizes end-of-school-year statuses for the selected year and authorized learner scope, with sorting and status views. EOSY status is recorded in learner records; enrollment/transfer status is a different field. Promotion and Retention pages act on learners already marked with the corresponding EOSY status. Do not claim that displaying a status report automatically promotes students or creates next-year enrollment. No individual status is available to EduAI unless explicitly authorized data is supplied, which this assistant's aggregate context does not include.

title: Reading Profile: CRLA and Phil-IRI
guidance: Reading Profile (/pages/reading-profile.html) separates Learner and Graphs views and supports filters and Export Excel. Grades 1–3 use CRLA: Grade Ready, Transitioning, Developing, High Emerging, Low Emerging. Grades 4–6 use Phil-IRI: Independent, Instructional, Frustration, Non reader. Record beginning/middle/end classifications through the learner editing workflow. Graph percentages are based on recorded assessments for each grade/period; missing values are not automatically low performance. EduAI may describe aggregate changes and suggest general classroom support, but must not identify struggling learners or infer individual reading results.

title: Math Profile and RMA classifications
guidance: Math Profile (/pages/math-profile.html) has Learner and Graphs views, filters, and Export Excel for the selected year and role scope. RMA values are recorded per BOSY/MOSY/EOSY. Categories include Not Proficient, Low Proficient, Nearly-Proficient, Proficient, and High-Proficient; the learner form may label the highest category Highly-Proficient, which chart normalization treats as equivalent. Compare supplied assessed counts and shares by period rather than inventing scores. Missing records mean no recorded classification. Guidance about interventions must be general suggestions, not an individual diagnosis or invented school policy.

title: Nutritional Status and nutrition charts
guidance: Nutritional Status (/pages/nutritional-status.html) has Learner and Graphs views, learner progress, filters, and Export Excel. Learner nutrition records include height, weight, and status at baseline/BOSY, midline/MOSY, and endline/EOSY. Status categories: Normal, Wasted, Severely Wasted, Overweight, Obese. Latest-status charts prefer endline, then midline, then baseline for each learner. Period charts use recorded assessments, so denominators may differ. EduAI only receives aggregate classifications/counts, never individual heights, weights, or health records. Do not diagnose or identify an individual from a chart; refer individual health concerns through the school's appropriate professional workflow.

title: Grades Profile and term-based grades
guidance: Grades Profile (/pages/grades-profile.html) offers term navigation, a subject-grades table, search/grade/program/gender filters, sorting, pagination, and Export Excel. Print Card is under Printables > Student Card. Subjects come from the selected year's grade-level curriculum assignments; no assigned subjects means none should be invented. Grading can be Numerical Grade or Letter Grade by year and grade level. Automatic Final Grade can be enabled or disabled per grade: when disabled, Final Grade is entered manually. Term count, passing threshold, rounding, grading type, and letter equivalents are school configuration, not universal constants. Ask a School Admin to correct configuration; staff should enter only the assigned subjects/terms and follow the form. EduAI does not receive individual grades.

title: Print Card workspace and SF9 learner performance card
guidance: From Printables choose Student Card, then Go to another page to Print Card; it opens /pages/print-card.html in a separate tab. Select year and learner, using grade/program/gender filters. The SF9 layout uses configured subjects for that learner's grade/year, saved term grades, the school logo, school/head information, and the year's adviser. The current SF9 template supports Numerical Grade only; Letter Grade disables printing/export and explains why. Print or export PDF, PNG, or Word .docx (the Word export contains the card as an image). Session-only corrections to card identity fields, letterhead, attendance, comments, signatures, and transfer certificate do not save back to learner/school records. Persistent corrections must be made through their management screens. Card template and attendance-layout administration belongs to School Admin Card Preferences, not the personal Preferences page.

title: Printables: Student Card, Good Moral, Certificate of Enrollment
guidance: Printables appears below Movement. Each page describes its document and opens a separate print studio. Student Card uses the existing Print Card studio. Good Moral and Certificate of Enrollment use the supplied MES templates with a fixed white background independent of theme. Choose school year, search/filter students, click a name to review information, and check students for one certificate per page. Student details, anecdotalRecords, school letterhead, schoolAddr, contactNumber, email, fbPage, school head, and school logo come from the selected school and learner records. Enter missing school address, issue date, or other details in Information; Good Moral fills the verified anecdotal record from the selected learner's saved anecdotalRecords field. Review it before printing; enter it manually only when missing. Edits stay in the open studio and do not update database records. School/footer edits apply to all certificates in the studio; student edits stay per student and year. Paper size, portrait/landscape, outer margin, document size, and preview-only zoom are adjustable. Reset layout returns to A4 portrait at original proportions. Print or export selected certificates to PDF or Word; Word contains page images. PNG exports the current preview. Disable browser headers/footers and print at 100%. Review missing fields before output; no documents are issued or signed automatically.

title: Promotion and retention
guidance: Movement → Promotion (/pages/promotion.html) lists learners whose source-year EOSY status is Promoted; Retention (/pages/retention.html) uses Retained. Select the source year, find the learner, and choose a configured succeeding school year, grade, section, and valid age. Retained learners must remain in the same grade; the target year must follow the source. Existing target-year LRNs block progression rather than being overwritten. Progression creates a target-year learner record and keeps source-year history; it is not deletion of the prior year. School Admins and Registrars can manage progression. Teachers require verified teacher-promotion permission and assigned coverage; if disabled/unverified, ask the School Admin. Do not treat a hidden/disabled action as permission to bypass checks.

title: Transfers, dropouts, archives and cancellation
guidance: Transfer Info (/pages/transfer-info.html) and Dropout Info (/pages/dropout.html) show dedicated movement/archive records under Movement. Record the relevant transfer type, school, date, reason/notes or EOSY dropout status through authorized learner workflows. Transferred-out/dropout records leave active enrollment and are stored in their corresponding year-scoped archives. Use the page's authorized cancellation action to return a movement record; cancellation checks for conflicts instead of overwriting an active record blindly. Deleting an archive entry sends it to Trash when supported. Data has separate Transferred Out and Dropout Info downloads. Teachers remain limited to assigned records. EduAI does not know an individual learner's movement history.

title: Data export workspace
guidance: Data (/pages/data.html) is a record download workspace, not database restore or student import. Select year and use search, grade, program, and gender filters; Refresh preview updates the visible records. Download filtered Excel and Download CSV follow the filters; Download full masterlist uses the whole authorized learner scope for that year. Download Transferred Out and Download Dropout Info export their archives. Large exports display progress and offer Cancel; changing filters does not make EduAI aware of the on-screen selection. Teachers export only their allowed scope. Files may contain sensitive student data and should stay with authorized school staff. Full-tenant JSON backup and bulk import require a School Admin.

title: Trash and restoration
guidance: Trash — /pages/trash.html stores supported removed learner/archive records by school year. Choose the year, Refresh if needed, inspect the source/removal information, and use Restore selected or Permanently delete selected, with confirmation. A School Admin can review all tenant Trash records; Teachers see only assigned grade/section records. Registrars do not have Trash access. Restore refuses conflicts with an existing record. Permanent deletion is irreversible. Trash retention can be 7, 15, 30 days, or Never; only an administrator changes it. Expiry depends on the configured purge process and is not a guarantee that an expired record is still recoverable.

title: Settings and personal account maintenance
guidance: Settings (/pages/settings.html) includes Account, Upload a Profile Photo, Remove photo, and Account Settings for the signed-in account's display name/password. Photo upload opens a crop/zoom step and uses configured Cloudinary unsigned uploads. A missing Cloudinary configuration must be fixed by the school's deployment administrator; a user should not paste API secrets into the page. Removing a photo clears its profile reference and does not promise deletion of the underlying Cloudinary asset. Personal account changes do not change your role, teaching assignments, another user's credentials, or school-wide settings. Admin Console appears only for School Admins.

title: Personal Preferences: themes and Learner Inspection
guidance: Personal Preferences (/pages/preferences.html) controls the account's theme and Learner Inspection action toggle. Themes include Light, Dark, Dracula, Monokai, Beach, Nord, Forest, and ClentIndustries Theme. Learner Inspection is on by default and controls showing the Inspect learner action; it is not a permission grant. Preferences does not configure report-card templates, school subjects, roles, term counts, or backups. If Inspect is hidden, check the personal toggle as well as role access.

title: Utilities page components and tools
guidance: The Utilities landing page /pages/utilities.html has Grade Calculator and BMI Calculator cards. Grade Calculator (/pages/grade-calculator.html) accepts subject grades from 60 to 100, excludes empty subjects, and calculates their arithmetic average; Calculate average and Clear do not save grades to student records. BMI Calculator (/pages/bmi-calculator.html) takes height in meters and weight in kilograms, computes weight divided by height squared, and has Calculate BMI and Clear. BMI is a screening measure; children need age- and sex-specific percentile interpretation, not an adult cutoff diagnosis. Data is a separate export workspace. EduAI is a separate AI assistant page, not a card on the Utilities landing page.

title: Website Feedback page and form
guidance: Website Feedback (/pages/feedback.html) is the sidebar's bottom Feedback link. It shows the signed-in email read-only, evaluation ratings with 1=Poor to 5=Excellent, and a required comment up to 2,000 characters. Submit feedback sends the response to the configured website administrator service. It does not change learner data, create an account, or open Trash. If submission fails, verify connectivity and ask the administrator to check the feedback endpoint. Avoid including student-private details in feedback.

title: Global search and finding page components
guidance: Use topbar global search with Ctrl+K on Windows/Linux or Command+K on macOS. Type a page, tool, or indexed component name, select a result, and jump to the indexed component when available. Arrow keys/Enter select results and Escape closes search. The search indexes available app controls; it is not a database search for every learner. Role-restricted results are filtered; direct URLs do not bypass role checks. On mobile the topbar menu opens the sidebar.

title: EduAI chat, conversation history and boundaries
guidance: EduAI (/pages/eduai.html) answers E-Dash usage questions and interprets supplied role-scoped school aggregates. Active School Admin, Registrar, or Teacher accounts need the school's EduAI entitlement. Use New chat or a saved conversation; older messages can be loaded and conversations deleted. Chat history belongs to the current user in the selected school. The assistant cannot click controls, upload files, edit/delete learners, change grades, create accounts, deploy rules, or complete a backup restore. It does not see open tabs, files, browser filters, private account data, individual grades, contact/guardian details, or health records. Names, if enabled, are name-only and bounded. Never treat zero permitted names as evidence of zero learners.

title: AI settings, providers, usage and errors
guidance: AI settings switches between shared Default Gemini and a personal provider account (Groq, OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Mistral, OpenRouter). Users select a supported provider/model and enter their key in the settings UI, never in chat. Keys are encrypted in gateway storage, not visible to EduAI. Settings include reply length, creativity, timeout, conversation history size, and learner-name limits; model availability and provider quotas come from that provider. Monthly requests/token totals are per user/provider. Reset role defaults resets only the user's preferences, not tenant permissions or everyone else's settings. Missing shared Gemini configuration, invalid credentials, model errors, timeouts, and quota/billing exhaustion are different failures; do not promise a free allowance or claim switching models resets quota. Never ask the user to reveal a key or service-account file.

title: Missing records, denied permissions and safe troubleshooting
guidance: For missing records: check selected school, school year, filters, and teacher assignment. Check whether the learner is in a transfer/dropout archive or authorized Trash instead of active enrollment. For permission denied: verify an active account and correct role, then ask the School Admin to check the tenant rules/deployment. Changing public Firebase Web App config or refreshing cannot grant permissions. Do not suggest allow-all rules, sharing another account, exposing service-account keys, or bypassing access checks. EduAI can explain an error message but cannot inspect live browser/network logs, uploaded files, or deployment state. If context lacks a fact, say what is unverified and identify the relevant owner/action.

title: Admin Console: accounts and school configuration
guidance: School Admins open Settings → Admin Console (/pages/manage-users.html). Manage Users is this console's account administration workspace. Its tabs are School structure, Card Preferences, Access management, Database backup, and Audit log; subgroups use collapsible panels. Choose the intended editing year before changing year-specific settings. The separate /pages/audit-log.html route also shows read-only activity history and is admin-gated. Personal Preferences (/pages/preferences.html) is for themes and Learner Inspection, not school-wide configuration. Roles/active status and tenant Firestore rules enforce access; a hidden control is not an invitation to bypass them.

title: School structure: school years and Make current
guidance: Admin Console → School structure: select Editing year to inspect/configure that year. Make current explicitly changes the school's current year; simply viewing a past year does not. Add school year requires a consecutive YYYY-YYYY range later than the latest configured year. The new year copies structural starting templates from the source/current year: sections without advisers, curriculum assignments, teacher assignments that still match copied sections, grade terms, and grade-level grading configuration. These remain editable; creating a year does not automatically enroll/promote learners or copy their scores. Use Promotion/Retention for learner progression.

title: School structure: grades, sections, advisers and teaching coverage
guidance: Admin Console → School structure manages configured sections for the editing year. Add section selects a supported grade (Kinder, Grades 1–6), section name, and adviser/teacher details; edit/remove actions apply to that structure. Access management → user editing assigns a Teacher's year-specific grade/section coverage, including multiple assignments and yearly history. A section existing does not by itself assign every teacher to it. Student forms and Import students must select configured placement; do not use an imported spreadsheet to invent sections. Verify teacher coverage when a teacher's class records or actions are missing.

title: School structure: grade terms, grading types, final grades and rounding
guidance: Admin Console → School structure configures Final grade rounding (nearest whole number, half up, or keep decimals), 1–4 grade terms plus Final Grade, a passing threshold, and grading type by grade level for the selected year. Numerical Grade uses numeric values; Letter Grade uses a validated letter-to-number range table. Add row edits that scale; save grade settings to persist it. Automatic Final Grade can be disabled per grade, requiring manual final-grade entry instead of averaging. Assign subjects by grade separately; a grading type does not assign subjects. Changes affect grade entry, profile calculations, and card behavior. The current SF9 print template supports numerical grading only. Do not change a grading configuration to force a particular learner's result.

title: School structure: curriculum subject pool and assignments
guidance: Admin Console → School structure → Assign subjects by grade lets the School Admin choose a grade and its subjects for the editing year, then Save grade subjects. Add to shared subject pool / Add subject adds a reusable subject definition; each grade/year still needs its own assignments. Subject pool definitions are tenant-wide, while assignments are year-specific. Grades Profile, learner grade entry, and Print Card use those assignments; do not fall back to unrelated static subjects when no assignments exist. Verify the year and grade before diagnosing missing grade columns or a card with no learning-area rows.

title: Card Preferences: templates and attendance layout
guidance: Admin Console → Card Preferences has three collapsible groups: Choose a card template (preview/full-screen inspection), Template by grade level, and Attendance layout. Configure supported template assignments, attendance months in display order, and row labels for Class days, Present, and Absent; Save preferences persists school settings. These controls configure the print workspace, not the personal theme. Currently the original numerical SF9 template is available; do not invent extra templates or letter-grade card support. Per-print learner identity/attendance/comment edits in Print Card are session-only and do not update Firestore learner records.

title: Access management: user directory and account lifecycle
guidance: Admin Console → Access management → User directory supports Add User, search, editing, and removal. Roles are School Admin, Registrar, and Teacher; Visitor is not a managed staff account. Add/edit uses full name, DepEd email, temporary password when creating, role, Active/status choice, and Teacher coverage by school year/grade/section. Assign only configured classes. Do not remove your own account; account removal requires a confirmed authorized operation and can involve separate Firebase Authentication and Firestore steps. Changing a role or coverage is a permissions change, not a theme preference. EduAI cannot see passwords, list private user profiles, create accounts, or verify whether a requested account was deleted.

title: Access management: Parent Portal, promotion and Trash retention
guidance: Admin Console → Access management configures Parent Portal access, Promotion & Retention for teachers, and Trash retention. Parent Portal enables/disables public parent lookup; it does not give a parent staff access. The teacher progression toggle allows assigned Teachers to use Promotion/Retention; it does not grant school-wide classes or administrator access. Trash retention choices are 7, 15, 30 days, or Never. A configured retention policy is distinct from whether a scheduled purge is deployed/running. Use applicationAccess.schoolSettings when verified; when unavailable do not guess current values. Defaults for a missing toggles document are Parent Portal on, teacher progression off, 30-day Trash retention, and nearest-integer rounding.

title: Tenant database backup, restore modes and review summary
guidance: Admin Console → Database backup → Tenant database backup is collapsible and starts closed. Export JSON downloads app-managed tenant users, school years, learners, archives/trash, settings, academic structure, assignment history, and public statistics; it excludes Firebase Authentication accounts/passwords and arbitrary collections. Choose Restore mode, then Restore JSON. Validation checks format/schema, selected school, supported paths, duplicates/types, and inclusion of the signed-in active School Admin. The on-page Backup summary shows filename, school, export date, mode, document/student/user/year totals and other record counts. Nothing is uploaded yet. Choose Review and restore, then final confirmation; a safety backup downloads first. Replace overwrites matching paths and deletes other managed records absent from the file; Merge updates supplied fields and preserves absent fields/records; Extend adds only missing paths. Restore is not atomic. Cancel restore discards preparation; changing mode clears the review and requires selecting the file again. Student-only datasets belong in Import students, not tenant restore.

title: Import students from JSON, CSV or merged-header spreadsheets
guidance: Admin Console → Database backup → Import students is a separate collapsible student-only workflow. Select school year, required Grade level and Section from that year's configured school structure; all imported students use this placement and file grade/section columns are ignored. Export template downloads example JSON for manual preparation. Import students reads content rather than extension: JSON/JSON Lines, CSV/TSV/other delimiters, XLS/XLSX/XLSB, ODS, Spreadsheet XML, HTML tables. Limits: 10 MB, 20,000 rows, 256 columns, 30 worksheets; one worksheet per import. Choose worksheet, date order (SF1 month/day/year or day/month/year), and Auto/1–5 header rows. Scan and validate finds LRN/name labels, combines merged parent/child headers, and skips SF1 totals/legend/signatures. It normalizes YYYY-MM-DD birthdates, age, names, sex, phones and booleans; guardian/contact missing or unavailable become N/A for future Masterlist editing. Anecdotal Records columns are supported; blank or absent values preserve existing saved records during matched updates. Name suffixes such as JR/Junior, SR/Senior, II, III, IV, and XII are separated from trailing name components and normalized into suffix. Suffix/Name extension/Name Ext. columns are supported. Comma names accept Last, First, Middle, Suffix and Last, First, Suffix, Middle; recognized suffix components are detected before assigning the middle name, regardless of spacing. Use an explicit suffix column or fourth comma-separated part for custom suffixes and single-letter Roman numerals to preserve initials. Matching repeated suffixes are deduplicated; conflicting suffixes or extra unrecognized comma components require source correction. Unknown fields are ignored. Errors, duplicate LRNs/labels, invalid values, wrong school/year metadata, or archived conflicts block upload. Review mappings/warnings/preview and prepared JSON. Existing LRNs default to Skip; Update matched fields preserves absent values/known contact details but assigns the chosen grade/section. Review and upload requires final confirmation, then shows Done and optional normalized JSON download. Changing placement requires rescanning. No deletions; interrupted uploads report saved progress.

title: Backup and import troubleshooting
guidance: A tenant JSON export/restore uses the signed-in School Admin's tenant Firestore permissions. For missing/insufficient permission, check the active users/{uid} role/status and publish the latest tenant firestore.rules to the selected school's project; editing the local rules file or central registry rules does not deploy them. Export errors identify the denied path/project. Do not solve this by putting service-account credentials in .env.local or allowing public database access. In Import students, no guardian/contact is allowed and becomes N/A; nonempty invalid phone values still need correction. Fix source-row errors and reselect/rescan the file. Changing grade/section or restore mode invalidates prior review. Files are parsed locally; EduAI does not receive or inspect their rows.

title: Audit log and activity history
guidance: Admin Console → Audit log and /pages/audit-log.html show read-only Activity history. Refresh log loads current entries; Previous/Next paginate with 10 per page. Search entries on this page filters only the loaded page, not the entire spreadsheet history. Audit integration uses the school's separately configured Apps Script endpoint; missing configuration or an outdated deployment can prevent loading. Publishing frontend code does not deploy Apps Script. Logs are evidence of recorded operations, not a guarantee every external action was captured. EduAI has workflow documentation, not live audit rows or private account activity.
